description: An original storybook settlement on flat ground. Ochre cottages line the older southern lane; a skewed western workshop quarter gathers around an orchard court; and a copper-domed archive anchors the northern bend beside the canal. Rooflines, building depths and narrow passages vary between these locally aligned groups.

imaginary.brief: Create Lanternwater Lanes, a fictional storybook canal village on a flat 180 metre square. Retain the idea of a copper-domed archive, workshops, cottages, market courts, orchard planting and a canal, but make a denser settlement that feels grown over time. Use 45–60 objects, including about 24–30 varied buildings arranged into three close clusters along a gently bending market lane and a short waterfront spine. Aim for about 25–35% summed building footprint coverage, with varied narrow gaps and occasional shared walls, while keeping useful routes clear. Include two small uneven gathering courts rather than a giant central square. Orient buildings to their nearby route and cluster; avoid identical rows, equal setbacks and right-angle symmetry. Let the canal or shore have a simple bent polygon outline. Place only a few useful trees and fixtures in leftover pockets. Keep all footprints inside the scene and avoid solid overlaps. Use original bounded geometry for the copper-domed archive and one workshop, with other roofs interpreted from authored facts. Reference real layout relationships creatively; this is fiction, not a copy of a real town.
